topic: CLAUDE.md multi-file organization, @imports, plugin overlay, monorepo patterns

claims.claim: @import syntax: CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using @path/to/import syntax; imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the parent CLAUDE.md.
claims.quote: CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using `@path/to/import` syntax. Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them.

claims.claim: Import recursion has a hard maximum depth of five hops; deeper chains are blocked or silently truncated.
claims.quote: Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of five hops.

claims.claim: Both relative and absolute paths are allowed; relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, NOT cwd - critical for shared templates in ~/.claude/common/.
claims.quote: Both relative and absolute paths are allowed. Relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory.

claims.claim: Home-relative imports via @~/ tilde expansion are supported and documented (example: @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md).
claims.quote:
# Individual Preferences
- @~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md

claims.claim: Remote URL imports (@https://...) are NOT officially supported; docs only cover local filesystem paths. Community workaround: git clone private repo + local import, or symlinks.
claims.quote: Oficjalna dokumentacja nie wspomina wsparcia dla `@https://example.com/rules.md`. Wszystkie przyklady w docs ograniczaja sie do local filesystem paths.

claims.claim: External-import approval dialog appears on first encounter with imports outside cwd; decline = permanent disable for the project, requiring manual settings edit to reverse.
claims.quote: The first time Claude Code encounters external imports in a project, it shows an approval dialog listing the files. If you decline, the imports stay disabled and the dialog does not appear again.

claims.claim: Circular @import detection is not explicitly documented in memory docs but is confirmed by community testing and exists analogously for skills loader ('Circular Dependency Detected' error).
claims.quote: When Claude Code initializes a skill, it walks the dependency tree before executing any code. The loader maintains a 'currently loading' set. If it encounters a skill that is already in that set, it knows a cycle exists and raises the error immediately rather than entering an infinite loop.

claims.claim: Circular symlinks in .claude/rules/ ARE officially documented as detected and handled gracefully - this is explicit for symlinks but not for @import.
claims.quote: Symlinks are resolved and loaded normally, and circular symlinks are detected and handled gracefully.

claims.claim: Missing imported files are silently skipped (no error); /memory command is recommended to verify loaded files.
claims.quote: Brak pliku: silent skip. Import jak @missing.md zostaje usuniety z kontekstu bez bledu, Claude po prostu nie widzi tego bloku.

claims.claim: Hierarchical discovery: Claude walks up the directory tree from cwd, loading every CLAUDE.md along the way (eager) and concatenating them into context rather than overriding.
claims.quote: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md files by walking up the directory tree from your current working directory... All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other.

claims.claim: Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files are LAZY-loaded - included only when Claude reads files in those subdirectories (not at launch). This is the killer feature for monorepos.
claims.quote: Claude also discovers CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files in subdirectories under your current working directory. Instead of loading them at launch, they are included when Claude reads files in those subdirectories.

claims.claim: Plugins do NOT provide their own CLAUDE.md; they contribute namespaced components (skills/agents/commands/hooks/MCP/settings) via plugin-name: prefix. Plugin overlay of project CLAUDE.md is a myth.
claims.quote: Brak CLAUDE.md w plugin root - plugin nie dostarcza persistent instructions do kontekstu.

claims.claim: Plugin settings.json takes priority over plugin.json settings; unknown keys silently ignored. Plugin hooks ADD to project hooks (sequential execution), not override.
claims.quote: Settings from settings.json take priority over settings declared in plugin.json. Unknown keys are silently ignored.

claims.claim: --plugin-dir local plugin takes precedence over marketplace plugin of same name for the session - key for plugin development flow.
claims.quote: When a --plugin-dir plugin has the same name as an installed marketplace plugin, the local copy takes precedence for that session.

claims.claim: Canonical monorepo pattern: lean root CLAUDE.md (~150-300 lines universal rules) + per-package CLAUDE.md in packages/*/CLAUDE.md loaded on-demand. Example: acme-platform Turborepo with api/web/shared packages.
claims.quote: Root CLAUDE.md content (abridged): Tech stack: Turborepo, Node 20, pnpm workspaces... Kazdy package CLAUDE.md zaweza scope: packages/api/CLAUDE.md: Express, Prisma, Zod, port 4000

claims.claim: Lazy subdir loading enables drastic startup context reduction: dev.to anvodev reported 47k words -> 9k words in main CLAUDE.md (~80-90% savings) by moving scoped content to packages.
claims.quote: Dev.to article anvodev reported reduction 47k words -> 9k words w main CLAUDE.md (-80%) poprzez przeniesienie scoped content do packages.

claims.claim: Virtual Monorepo pattern (Medium/DevOps AI) for firms with 35+ independent repos: workspace/ with each subfolder as independent git repo, root CLAUDE.md describes interconnections for cross-service reasoning.
claims.quote: Kazdy subfolder to niezalezny git repo (teams keep their workflows). Root CLAUDE.md opisuje interconnections

claims.claim: 5 splitting strategies: (1) per topic - doc-per-concern in agent_docs/ with Claude choosing which to read; (2) per audience - AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md pattern for multi-agent compat; (3) per lifecycle - persistent CLAUDE.md vs ephemeral plans/; (4) per path scope - .claude/rules/ with YAML paths: frontmatter; (5) per agent persona - move multi-step procedures to skills/agents.
claims.quote: Include a list of these files with a brief description of each, and instruct Claude to decide which (if any) are relevant and to read them before it starts working.

claims.claim: Per-audience pattern: Claude reads CLAUDE.md not AGENTS.md; if repo uses AGENTS.md for other coding agents (Cursor/Copilot/Codex), create CLAUDE.md that imports it (@AGENTS.md) to avoid duplication.
claims.quote: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md. If your repository already uses AGENTS.md for other coding agents, create a CLAUDE.md that imports it so both tools read the same instructions without duplicating them.

claims.claim: .claude/rules/*.md with YAML frontmatter paths: glob are LAZY-loaded only when Claude reads matching files; rules WITHOUT paths: are eager - key distinction for token budget.
claims.quote: Kluczowa roznica vs @imports: rules bez paths: ladowane sa unconditionally na starcie sesji (zjadaja kontekst); rules z paths: ladowane lazownie tylko gdy Claude czyta pliki pasujace do glob pattern.

claims.claim: Loading precedence order: (1) managed policy CLAUDE.md (cannot be excluded), (2) user rules, (3) user CLAUDE.md, (4) project CLAUDE.md (parent->cwd), (5) project rules, (6) CLAUDE.local.md, (7) lazy subdir CLAUDE.md, (8) auto memory, (9) conversation. CLAUDE.local.md appended after CLAUDE.md at same level.
claims.quote: Within each directory, CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md, so when instructions conflict, your personal notes are the last thing Claude reads at that level.

claims.claim: Conflicts between rules are resolved probabilistically - 'If two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily.' Explicit override wording required in lower-level files.
claims.quote: If two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily.

claims.claim: 4-layer organization model: L1 Universal (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, just me), L2 Project-wide (./CLAUDE.md, team via git), L3 Module-specific (packages/*/CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/, lazy), L4 Task-specific (plans/CURRENT.md, ephemeral).
claims.quote: L1 Universal | ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md | Ja w kazdym projekcie | Personal coding preferences... L4 Task-specific | plans/CURRENT.md | Biezacy task/feature

claims.claim: claudeMdExcludes in settings (user/project/local/managed) uses glob patterns against absolute file paths; arrays merge across layers. Managed policy CLAUDE.md CANNOT be excluded.
claims.quote: Patterns are matched against absolute file paths using glob syntax. You can configure claudeMdExcludes at any settings layer: user, project, local, or managed policy. Arrays merge across layers.

claims.claim: --add-dir by default gives file access but does NOT load CLAUDE.md from that dir; env var CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 enables cross-repo CLAUDE.md loading.
claims.quote: CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 claude --add-dir ../shared-config

claims.claim: Shared template strategies: (1) ~/.claude/common/ with @ imports in global CLAUDE.md; (2) private GitHub repo cloned to ~/company-rules/ + cron sync; (3) symlinks in .claude/rules/; (4) managed policy via MDM/Ansible; (5) plugin distribution (but plugin cannot provide CLAUDE.md).
claims.quote: Dla zespolow (nie-oficjalnie wspierany ale powszechny): Firma tworzy repo acme-corp/claude-code-standards (private), Developers klonuja do ~/acme-standards/, Cron / post-receive hook syncuje

claims.claim: Project-root CLAUDE.md survives /compact (re-read from disk and re-injected); nested subdir CLAUDE.md files are NOT re-injected automatically - they reload next time Claude reads files in that subdir.
claims.quote: Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session. Nested CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories are not re-injected automatically; they reload the next time Claude reads a file in that subdirectory.

claims.claim: Block-level HTML comments (<!-- ... -->) in CLAUDE.md are stripped before context injection - useful for maintainer notes without token cost. Comments in code blocks are NOT stripped.
claims.quote: Block-level HTML comments (<!-- maintainer notes -->) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context.

claims.claim: CLAUDE.local.md is NOT deprecated despite GitHub issue #2950 confusion; current docs still describe it as 'loaded alongside CLAUDE.md and treated the same way.' Community trend favors @~/.claude/... imports for worktree portability.
claims.quote: For private per-project preferences that shouldn't be checked into version control, create a CLAUDE.local.md at the project root. It loads alongside CLAUDE.md and is treated the same way.

claims.claim: Import graph hop counting example: CLAUDE.md(0) -> AGENTS.md(1) -> conventions.md(2) -> glossary.md(3), safely within 5-hop limit. Typical patterns use only 2 hops; 5-hop limit mostly affects meta-templates with N levels of delegation.
claims.quote: Hops od root: CLAUDE.md (0) -> AGENTS.md (1) -> conventions.md (2) -> glossary.md (3). Bezpiecznie w limicie 5.

gaps_flagged: Remote URL imports: not officially supported, most-requested feature, no native alternative
Exact error mode at 6+ hops: silent truncation vs warning vs hard error - no spec
Circular @import error message: community confirms detection but not in official memory docs (only for skills/symlinks)
Plugin-provided CLAUDE.md: not possible by design, feature request candidate for Next.js-style project configs
@import in CLAUDE.local.md: implied by 'treated the same way' but not explicitly confirmed
Interaction of @import with claudeMdExcludes: which wins is unconfirmed
Relative path with .. upward traversal: probably allowed but external-import dialog may trigger
Max single imported file size: no hard limit documented (200 lines is recommendation only)
Async reload: whether /memory after /compact shows updated list
Layered precedence empirical tests: formal definition for edge cases like user rule with paths: vs project rule without paths
